mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best expresses the qualitative statement of the second law of thermodynamics?

options.A: Heat can spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
options.B: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
options.C: Work can be completely converted into heat without any loss.
options.D: Energy can be created or destroyed in a cyclic process.

mcqs.answer: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
mcqs.explanation: The second law states that heat does not flow spontaneously from a colder to a hotter body; it flows naturally from higher to lower temperature. Option B captures this qualitative statement. Options A and D contradict the law, and C describes the first law, not the second.

mcqs.question: Two bodies, one at 300 K and the other at 350 K, are placed in thermal contact. In which direction will heat flow spontaneously?

options.A: From the 300 K body to the 350 K body
options.B: From the 350 K body to the 300 K body
options.C: No net heat flow because the temperatures are close
options.D: Heat will flow back and forth equally

mcqs.answer: From the 350 K body to the 300 K body
mcqs.explanation: Heat always flows spontaneously from the higher‑temperature body to the lower‑temperature body. Hence it moves from 350 K to 300 K. Option A reverses the direction, while C and D ignore the temperature gradient.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the limitation on the efficiency of any heat engine operating between two thermal reservoirs?

options.A: Its efficiency can be 100% if the engine is ideal.
options.B: Its efficiency can exceed that of a Carnot engine between the same reservoirs.
options.C: Its efficiency cannot exceed that of a Carnot engine operating between the same reservoirs.
options.D: Its efficiency is independent of the temperatures of the reservoirs.

mcqs.answer: Its efficiency cannot exceed that of a Carnot engine operating between the same reservoirs.
mcqs.explanation: The second law imposes that no real engine can be more efficient than a reversible (Carnot) engine working between the same hot and cold reservoirs. Option C states this. Options A and B violate the second law, and D ignores the temperature dependence.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following processes is (approximately) reversible?

options.A: Free expansion of a gas into a vacuum
options.B: Slow, frictionless movement of a piston with infinitesimal pressure difference
options.C: Mixing of two different gases in a container
options.D: Heat flow across a finite temperature difference

mcqs.answer: Slow, frictionless movement of a piston with infinitesimal pressure difference
mcqs.explanation: A reversible process proceeds through a series of equilibrium states; a slow, frictionless piston with an infinitesimal pressure difference satisfies this. Free expansion, mixing, and heat flow across a finite ΔT are irreversible because they generate entropy and cannot be undone without external effects.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following real‑world examples best illustrates the qualitative statement of the second law of thermodynamics?

options.A: Ice melting at 0 °C when placed in a room at 25 °C
options.B: Heat flowing spontaneously from a cold ice cube to warm water
options.C: A refrigerator cooling its interior while consuming electrical work
options.D: A perpetual‑motion machine that produces work without any heat input

mcqs.answer: Ice melting at 0 °C when placed in a room at 25 °C
mcqs.explanation: The ice absorbs heat from the warmer surroundings and melts, showing heat flowing naturally from a hotter body (room) to a colder one (ice). This aligns with the second law. Option B reverses the natural direction, C involves external work, and D is impossible under the second law.

mcqs.question: A metal rod at 400 K is placed in contact with another identical rod at 300 K. After a short time, which statement correctly describes the heat flow?

options.A: Heat flows from the 300 K rod to the 400 K rod
options.B: Heat flows from the 400 K rod to the 300 K rod
options.C: No heat flows because the rods are identical
options.D: Heat flows equally in both directions

mcqs.answer: Heat flows from the 400 K rod to the 300 K rod
mcqs.explanation: Heat always moves from the higher temperature object to the lower temperature one until thermal equilibrium is reached. Therefore it flows from 400 K to 300 K. Options A, C, and D contradict this principle.

mcqs.question: A student claims: "A heat engine can convert all the heat it absorbs from the hot reservoir into useful work, leaving no waste heat." Is this statement correct?

options.A: Yes, if the engine is perfectly efficient
options.B: No, because some heat must always be rejected to a cold reservoir
options.C: Yes, but only for engines operating at very low temperatures
options.D: No, because work cannot be produced from heat

mcqs.answer: No, because some heat must always be rejected to a cold reservoir
mcqs.explanation: The second law requires that a heat engine must discharge some heat to a colder sink; 100 % conversion of heat to work is impossible. Option B states this limitation. Option A ignores the second law, C is false, and D misstates the first law.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about entropy change is true?

options.A: In a reversible process, the total entropy change of system plus surroundings is positive
options.B: In an irreversible process, the total entropy change of system plus surroundings is zero
options.C: In a reversible process, the total entropy change of system plus surroundings is zero
options.D: In both reversible and irreversible processes, the total entropy change is always negative

mcqs.answer: In a reversible process, the total entropy change of system plus surroundings is zero
mcqs.explanation: For a reversible (ideal) process, the entropy increase of the system is exactly balanced by the entropy decrease of the surroundings, giving a net zero change. Irreversible processes produce a positive net entropy increase. Options A and B invert the correct relationship, and D is never true.
